noticias.titulo: the search for a home without a fixed address, from prefabricated houses to floating dwellings
noticias.resumo: THE IDEA OF A HOME WITHOUT A FIXED ADDRESS   For decades, architects have imagined homes that can be packed up , transported, and assembled somewhere new, designing alternatives to the idea that housing must be tied to…
noticias.trecho: THE IDEA OF A HOME WITHOUT A FIXED ADDRESS   For decades, architects have imagined homes that can be packed up , transported, and assembled somewhere new, designing alternatives to the idea that housing must be tied to a permanent address. From prefabricated dwellings designed for mass production to experimental houses conceived for remote landscapes, these projects explore how architecture might exist beyond the limits of a fixed site.   One early expression of this ambition came from American architect and inventor Buckminster Fuller. In 1928, he developed the concept for the Dymaxion House, a prefabricated dwelling conceived for mass production and delivery as a single unit by aircraft. Its lightweight aluminum structure reflected Fuller’s interest in applying industrial manufacturing to housing. Although the project never developed into a commercially viable housing system, it…

noticias.resumo: Kodak has reported a third quarter with higher revenue, higher profit, and less debt, and CEO Jim Continenza told investors that the company continues “to see growth in motion picture films.” Two days later, Universal…
noticias.trecho: Kodak has reported a third quarter with higher revenue, higher profit, and less debt, and CEO Jim Continenza told investors that the company continues “to see growth in motion picture films.” Two days later, Universal confirmed that Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, shot completely on KODAK 65mm film, returns to theaters on December 11. The two announcements are not connected, and Kodak’s CEO did not mention The Odyssey on the call. Together they still answer a question we asked fifteen months ago, when  Kodak warned about its ability to continue as a going concern . The main supplier of motion picture camera film is in a much safer financial position, and the largest film-originated release of the year is still earning money for the format. noticias.titulo: Carling’s new identity is a badge of belonging inspired by its football ties
noticias.resumo: BrandOpus has refreshed the much-loved lager brand with a football-style crest celebrating its Burton brewing heritage and its mission of “bringing mates together”. In the last decade or so, it feels like every British…
noticias.trecho: BrandOpus has refreshed the much-loved lager brand with a football-style crest celebrating its Burton brewing heritage and its mission of “bringing mates together”. In the last decade or so, it feels like every British brand has tried to link itself with British football. But some have been in the game, so to speak, longer than others. And if you’re looking for authentic ties, you’ll struggle to find a better example than Carling. For decades now, it’s been in the hands of fans on matchday, and despite the inexorable rise of hipster craft beers, this honest, reliable, easy-drinking, thirst-quenching amber nectar of a drink (can you tell it’s my favourite tipple?) still gets great love from the football crowd today. That love has long been two-way. Carling’s name has been on cup competitions, club hoardings and more than a few pub chalkboards for as long as I can remember. And in 2026…

referencias.trecho: In Shanghai’s Jing’an Sculpture Park, a monumental new installation by Brooklyn’s Wade and Leta has a clear goal: to get people up and moving in the same space. Titled “Catching Feelings,” the interactive artwork doubles as an all-ages playground with the artists’ signature sculptures and geometric forms. A central tower holds a quartet of slides, while other spinning and writhing elements are designed for more unstructured interaction. “Catching Feelings” is one of 36 projects in the ninth edition of the Jing’an International Sculpture Project, an annual project helmed by the UCCA Center for Contemporary Art . referencias.trecho: An extraordinary student film from Australia’s AFTRS , Interview With a Hero sees its co-writer and director, Celeste Diep , plumb her family history to tell a moving immigrant story set in 1990s Sydney. A daughter who feels distant from her father due to his work and guarded stoicism witnesses him struggle with the traumas he experienced during the genocidal reign of Cambodia’s Khmer Rouge. The father, Chhay, is a practitioner of traditional Cambodian shadow puppetry , and the short opens with him performing a scene from one of the shows, which appear popular and well attended among the Cambodian diaspora. Afterward, an attractive white television reporter approaches Chhay and invites him to perform on her television show. Though he accepts, the opportunity seems to bother him, and he seeks reassurance from community leaders. The scenes leading up to the TV performance highlight both…

referencias.titulo: Haunted Histories, Living Ghosts: Celeste Diep Explores Cambodia’s Generational Wounds in ‘Interview with a Hero’
referencias.resumo: The weight of history is not always something that can be spoken about, but it can be shown, or it can come out in unexpected ways or times. For many Cambodian people, the trauma of the Khmer Rouge regime, the genocide…
referencias.trecho: The weight of history is not always something that can be spoken about, but it can be shown, or it can come out in unexpected ways or times. For many Cambodian people, the trauma of the Khmer Rouge regime, the genocide and the generations of silence that followed remain an ever-present burden, passed down through families and carried into everyday life. In Celeste Diep’s Australian Film Television and Radio School (AFTRS) short film Interview with a Hero , that inherited pain becomes the starting point for a deeply affecting story about generational trauma and diaspora, centred on Chhay, a man whose buried past threatens his relationships with his family and community. The short caught my eye some time ago, and was part of my SXSW London selection, so it feels completely natural to welcome the film to our pages for its premiere. Recently, Taz F. biblioteca.trecho: Os processos de colocação em discurso com tecnologias de inteligência artificial generativa no site Dall-e 2 são analisados a partir das proposições da semiótica acerca das interações discursivas. As projeções no enunciado de um ator humano e de um ator maquínico produzem efeitos de sentido de interações bilaterais reflexivas e unidirecionais entre esses atores que requerem novas competências do destinatário para um fazer interpretativo. Destaca-se a necessidade da identificação dessas marcas discursivas por parte do enunciatário para o estabelecimento dos contratos de comunicação.

bolhas.titulo: Religion and agriculture: More connected than you thought
bolhas.resumo: Heather Dawn Thompson When I think about what is different from Indigenous and western agricultural systems I think about monoculture and pesticides and fertilizers.  But I also think about religion. Our religion…
bolhas.trecho: Heather Dawn Thompson When I think about what is different from Indigenous and western agricultural systems I think about monoculture and pesticides and fertilizers.  But I also think about religion. Our religion, spirituality, and worldview shape how we navigate the world – and that includes food and agriculture.  MaLakota (I am Lakota) enrolled with Cheyenne River Sioux Tribe. In Lakota spirituality we believe in Mitakuye Oyasin ( mee-tah-koo-yay oh-yah-seen ): Roughly translated it means, “We are all related.” We say it after every prayer, before every meal, during every ceremony. It is at the heart of our “religion” or spirituality, and our worldview. Mitakuye Oyasin . We are all related. And not just we humans are related: all of us, the birds, the buffalo, the wind, the rocks, the bugs, the trees, the plants, the soil, the waters. We are all relatives, we are all related, we are…

bolhas.trecho: After Documenta 15, Taring Padi’s newfound prominence led them to engage in broader solidarity efforts around global issues such as colonialism and the Palestinian struggle. Part III of our interview series discusses the Indonesian collective’s recent works in their third and final chapter of “Rakyat Pasti Menang” at Ibraaz London, which closes on November 22.  The interview was conducted with Alexander Supartono, a first-generation member of Taring Padi and an associate professor at Edinburgh Napier University. Follow the links for Part I and Part II to read the full conversation.
